macro.headline: Dow leads to record highs; tech lags as rotation broadens into cyclicals and healthcare.
macro.story:
The facts first: SPY sits at $744.78, above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, up 1.4% over the last five days but still down 1.7% over 21 days — a shallow pullback within an uptrend. The Dow closed at a record 52,900 (+1.9% in 5d, +3.1% in 21d) and its RSI has pushed to 70.2, an overbought reading. QQQ tells a different story: down 0.5% in 5d and down 4.4% in 21d, RSI 48.3, with a bearish MACD histogram — tech is the laggard. VIX is at 15.96, down 13% in five days, and breadth shows 44.8% bullish vs 29.4% bearish across the S&P 500 with 8 of 11 GICS sectors above their 50-day. WTI oil is deeply oversold (RSI 28.3, -28.9% in 21d), gold and silver are below both key moving averages, and the 10Y-2Y spread has compressed 52% in 21d to just 0.20.

On the causal side, the tracked conversation leans firmly bullish and attributes the price action to a widening rally led by the Dow and cyclicals. Sentiment is highlighting the Dow's record close as evidence that the bid is broadening beyond mega-cap tech, with the dominant view framing global market cap at a record $166 trillion as a continuation of the AI-driven bull cycle. At the same time, the tracked conversation is flagging genuine tail risks — a stark divergence between nonfarm payrolls and the household survey, and elevated leverage in both South Korean ETFs and US levered-ETF rebalancing flows. These are framed as risk-context, not immediate sell triggers. This narrative is broadly consistent with the sector data: Industrials, Financials, Healthcare and Utilities lead while Technology and Energy lag — a classic broadening move, not a defensive one. No clear attribution in today's tracked sentiment for the oil breakdown specifically, though the active themes data (not live sentiment) points to geopolitical risk unwind as a candidate driver.

Rotation-wise, the interesting hunting ground is Healthcare and Financials. Healthcare's Diagnostics & Research and Health Information Services industries both carry validated Early-Runway rotation tailwinds — early in a hot spell, top-decile relative strength. Credit Services (Financials) shares the same setup. Meanwhile the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 is neutral-to-weak with bearish MACD — a real conflict with the broad bull tape, and the reason confidence here is MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

Forward watch: the 10Y-2Y compression toward zero and the payrolls/household-survey divergence are the two structural warnings under the surface. Near-term, watch whether QQQ can reclaim its short-term momentum (MACD histogram is still negative) — if tech joins the cyclical bid, this becomes a HIGH-confidence broad advance; if tech breaks down while the Dow stays extended at RSI 70, expect a rotational chop.

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
active.evidence: WTI crude ~$80 (-~5% from recent highs); crude trajectory shifting from HOLDING_BULLISH toward FADING_BULLISH/bearish. Natural gas divergence intact (independent supply story — not demand-driven). Broad commodity complex already fading (DBC, USO, BNO).

invalidators.condition: Iran deal collapses or Hormuz incidents resume — crude reverses sharply higher
OPEC+ emergency production cut to defend $80 floor offsets supply increase

**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength is the dominant force this week, and it is quietly re-pricing everything sensitive to it. DXY at 100.78 is up 1.27% over 21 days, sitting above both its 21d and 50d SMAs with RSI 56.8 — a clean rising trend, not a spike. The ACTIVE DXY_METALS_TAG signal is doing exactly what the backtest says it should: Gold -5.8%, Silver -14.6%, Copper -4.1% over 21d, with the Precious Metals theme now flagged FADING. Every other cross-current — the health-care-led rotation, the AI compute chase, the oil collapse — is being filtered through a firmer dollar.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop is transitional but not hostile: regime CHOPPY (6/10), VIX 15.97 in contango with VIX3M at 20.13, breadth 72.7% of sectors above 50SMA, and S&P 5d breadth 54% bullish vs 27% bearish. 10Y yield 4.37% is below its lower Bollinger with RSI 40 — but per our backtest, do not fade this; yields have continued higher 53% of the time after such signals, so treat it as a trend read, not a reversal setup. Oil at 68.32 with RSI 28.9 is likewise a trend, not a bounce trigger (WTI oversold edge = -3.87%). The DXY signal is the one with real edge, and it's live.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Leadership is defensive-plus-financials, not classic risk-on: XLV +12.3%, XLF +8.5%, XLI +5.8%, XLU +4.9% over 21d, while XLY is flat and SPY itself is -1.7%. Rotation flows are going Into Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and unmapped names — the AI Infrastructure theme is in CHASING stage at day 32, health 8/10. Nothing is rotating OUT in size, but the tape is clearly narrowing: money is concentrating in health care and select compute names, while broad commodities and metals bleed.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The leaders that have already run are Semiconductors (HOT 13 months, +258% — record territory, CEILING flagged) and Medical Care Facilities (HOT 8 months, +43%); those are exit-management zones, not entry zones. The in-range setups with smart-money flow are inside the semis complex itself — SITM (coil 85%), MU (coil 75%), AMD (coil 97%), all LEAN BULLISH and under 10% moves on 5d/21d — plus UPST in Credit Services (coil 90%). Software - Infrastructure is only 1 month into a HOT spell with +3% gain (typical spell runs 7 months to +18%), so that's early-innings versus the extended semis index. Internet Content & Info is similarly 1 month in and -5% — early, not late.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is DXY 101.80 resistance. A break above extends the dollar trend and keeps pressure on Gold/Silver/Copper and by extension the commodity-reflation and precious-metals themes that are already fading. A rejection back below the 21d SMA (~99.7 area, near 99.38 support) would be the first real crack in the spine and would open the door for metals and broad risk to breathe. Secondary watch: VIX3M 20.13 holding contango — if that inverts, the CHOPPY regime tilts risk-off fast.
